title: What the UN Security Council Does and How It Votes

content: The United Nations Security Council is responsible for maintaining international peace and security. It has 15 members: five permanent and ten elected for two-year terms.
The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States. Each holds a veto, which means a resolution cannot pass if any one of them votes against it.
Decisions need at least nine votes in favour. Critics say the veto can block action on major crises, while supporters argue it keeps great powers engaged in the system.
